title: IVR decoder
blurb: End-to-end two-peer loopback where the caller sends tones via standard RTCRtpSender.dtmf and the receiving peer decodes the remote audio track with an 8-frequency Goertzel filter bank to drive an IVR menu.
question: Does DTMF sent through standard RTCRtpSender.dtmf survive end-to-end RFC 4733 transmission and receiver-side audio playout so a remote Goertzel filter bank can decode every digit?
result: Verified in Chrome 153 headless on both desktop and mobile across repeated runs: auto-test sent '14321#' and decoded '14321#' verbatim, and pressing '2' navigated the IVR menu to support. Cross-engine receiver playout on Firefox/Safari is unverified.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (desktop 1280x800 and mobile 360x740); not verified in Chrome 160, Firefox, or Safari

friction.summary: Loopback DTMF tones are only transmitted when the sending audio track carries active frames, and in-band tone regeneration on the receiving side is engine-dependent
friction.repro: Send RFC 4733 telephone-events over a loopback without an active audio source or inspect the remote MediaStreamTrack in an engine that does not regenerate in-band audio playout from telephone-events; the Goertzel decoder reads silence.
friction.workaround: Feed a silent Web Audio oscillator into MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode on the sender, keep the tab in the foreground to avoid timer throttling, and surface sent vs decoded mismatches honestly.
